_comment: One entry in builtin:openpipeline.metrics.routing, created by hand once.
WHY BY HAND. The extension package installs the pipeline itself - it is declared in
extension.yaml and arrives with the zip. What it cannot install is this: a routing entry
on the BUILT-IN metrics ingest. An extension's own openpipeline source routes the
extension's own metrics, and host metrics are not the extension's metrics. Without this
entry the pipeline exists, the sync workflow fills its tables, and no record ever reaches
it - which looks exactly like a lookup table that did not work.
THE MATCHER MUST NOT REFERENCE cohesity_protectiongroup_id. That field is created inside
the pipeline by the first processor, so gating entry on it means no record ever arrives
and the lookup never runs. metric.key is present before any processing and is the only
safe thing to match on here.
WHY dt.host.cpu.usage. The rule needs a host metric that (a) exists on every
OneAgent-monitored host, (b) carries dt.smartscape.host, and (c) is ONE key rather than a
family, so the volume routed through the pipeline is one series per host rather than
dozens. A broader matcher costs pipeline throughput and buys nothing: the edge is drawn
from the first matching record and refreshed by every one after it.
pipelineId is the SETTINGS OBJECT ID of the installed pipeline, not its customId
('extension:cohesity-host-link'). See dynatrace/README.md for how to read it off the
description: Route host CPU metrics to the Cohesity host-link pipeline
